scenario.title: The Dome Turned at Midnight
scenario.setting_summary: A small telescope station on Kongma Ridge in Ladakh, winter 1998. Snow has closed the only road for three days.
background: Kongma Ridge Observatory sits at 4,600 metres in Ladakh. The year is 1998.
Four staff live here through winter. A cook and a truck driver are stuck here too.
Tonight they were meant to photograph a comet and send the plates to Delhi.
The station head was Dr Anil Verma, aged 52. He was strict, polite and very private.
At 10:40 pm every light in the station went out. At 11:15 pm Verma was found dead in the dome.
Snow has blocked the road for three days. The radio is the only way out.
Everyone here knows the dome is heavy. It only turns if someone switches off the safety lock first.

public_timeline.event: All six people eat dinner together in the mess.
Dr Verma walks up to the dome alone to open the shutter.
Every light in the station goes out at once.
The cook finds Dr Verma dead under the dome counterweight.
The radio will not reach Leh. Snow is still falling.

scenario.opening_scene: Wind pushes against the steel walls. The lights come back on, yellow and weak. In the dome, Dr Verma lies under the big counterweight, his glasses broken beside him. The shutter is open and snow is drifting in onto his coat. The road is shut. The radio is dead. Six people stand in a cold circle and nobody says anything for a long time.
scenario.case_question: Who killed Dr Anil Verma in the dome, and why?

truth.summary: The station head was not Anil Verma. He was Arvind Sahni, who stole the dead Verma's name after a lab fire in Pune in 1979. Himanshu Raikar came to the station to prove it, because that fire took his family. Tonight he found the proof, was confronted, hit the man with the dome counterweight pin, pulled the generator fuse, and turned the dome by hand so it looked like an accident.

timeline.event: A fire kills the real Anil Verma at a Pune lab. Arvind Sahni takes his papers and his name.
Himanshu Raikar joins the station as radio operator, using his mother's family name.
The station head grows suspicious of Himanshu and writes to Pune about his real name.
The station head takes one glass plate from the darkroom to check the dome safety panel.
Dinner. Everyone eats together. The mood is cold.
The station head goes up to the dome alone.
Himanshu stops writing the radio log and opens the office safe with a copied key.
Himanshu finds the 1979 clipping and the old medical letter. He takes them to the dome.
In the dome they argue. The man admits the name and says Himanshu will be sent off the mountain.
Himanshu hits him once with the brass counterweight pin. The man dies.
Himanshu runs to the shed and pulls the main fuse by hand so nobody comes up.
Himanshu turns the dome with the hand crank, after switching off the safety lock, so the counterweight rests on the body.
Himanshu pushes the fuse back and returns to the radio room.
The cook climbs to the dome and finds the body.

truth.method: One blow with the brass counterweight pin, then the dome was turned by hand onto the body to fake an accident.
truth.motive: Revenge. The dead man stole a dead scientist's name and left Himanshu's family to burn in 1979.
truth.ambiguities: Three other people hid things that night: sold data, a torn dismissal letter, and a forged medical licence. Any of them looks guilty for a while.

players.public_info: Himanshu Raikar keeps the station radio and writes the night log.
players.private_info: Himanshu wanted one thing for nineteen years: proof. A lab fire in Pune in 1979 took his family, and the man who walked away from it took a dead scientist's name, Anil Verma. Himanshu joined this station in 1996 under his mother's surname to find that proof. Tonight at 10:15 pm he opened the office safe with a copied key and found a 1979 clipping and an old medical letter. He carried them to the dome, they argued, and at 10:35 pm he hit the man once with the brass counterweight pin. Then he pulled the generator fuse by hand at 10:38 pm, turned the dome with the crank at 10:52 pm so the weight sat on the body, pushed the fuse back at 11:00 pm, and went back to the radio room.

key_deductions.statement: The death was not an accident. He was hit first, then the dome was turned onto him.
The darkness was made on purpose. Someone walked to the shed and pulled the fuse by hand.
The station head was not Anil Verma. He used a dead man's name from 1979.
The head was quietly checking his staff's papers and names before he died.
Only someone with a copied safe key and a gap in the log could reach the safe that night.
Rishabh's sacking and Nikhil's data money are real secrets but not the night's motive.

phases.name: Round 1: The Dark Hour
phases.objective: Find out how the lights went out and where each person stood.
try: Check the fuse box in the generator shed.
Read the night log times in the radio room.
Ask the cook who sat in the mess.
phases.planned_beat: The generator coughs and the lights flicker again. Everyone must say where they were at 10:40 pm.
phases.question: How did every light go out at 10:40 pm?
options: Someone pulled the main fuse out by hand
A storm surge blew the fuse
The dome motor shorted the station
phases.reward: The fuse was pulled at 10:38 pm and pushed back at about 11:00 pm.
phases.wrong_nudge: Look at the fuse itself. A blown fuse is black. This one is clean and off its clips.

phases.name: Round 2: The Name on the Door
phases.objective: Work out what the station head kept in his safe and why.

Check the letter book carbon in the radio room.
Ask the driver about the last post bag.
phases.planned_beat: The safe is found open. A 1979 clipping and an old letter are missing their envelope.
phases.question: Why was the station head keeping papers from a 1979 fire?
options: Because he was using the name of a man who died in that fire
Because he wanted an insurance payout
Because a mining firm was blackmailing him
Because he planned to sack his deputy
phases.reward: The real Anil Verma died in the Pune lab fire in 1979.
phases.wrong_nudge: Compare the photo on the old letter with the man in the dome. The names do not match.

phases.name: Round 3: Turning the Dome
phases.objective: Work out exactly how the body ended up under the counterweight.
try: Look at the safety lock and the crank marks.
Weigh the pin found on the dome floor.
Match the log gap to the dome timings.
phases.planned_beat: Snow melts off the dome rail and shows fresh crank scratches. The accident story falls apart.
phases.question: What actually happened to him in the dome?
options: He was hit with the brass pin, then the dome was cranked onto him
The counterweight slipped and crushed him
He fell from the ladder onto the rail
He was pushed out of the open shutter and dragged back
phases.reward: The dome was turned by hand at about 10:52 pm, after the blow was struck.
phases.wrong_nudge: The safety lock was off and the motor was dead. A dome cannot turn itself in the dark.

result.reveal_story: Here is the truth. The station head was not Dr Anil Verma. He was Arvind Sahni. The real Verma died in a Pune lab fire in 1979, and Sahni took his name and papers. That fire also killed Himanshu Raikar's family. Himanshu came here in 1996 under his mother's surname to prove it. At 10:15 pm he opened the safe with a copied key and found the 1979 clipping and an old letter. He carried them to the dome. The man admitted the name and said Himanshu would be sent off the mountain. At 10:35 pm Himanshu hit him once with the brass pin. He pulled the fuse at 10:38, cranked the dome onto the body at 10:52, pushed the fuse back at 11:00, and later faked his log. Rishabh's torn sacking letter, Nikhil's data money and Noor's bought licence were all real secrets, but none of them killed anyone. Himanshu and Noor were secretly married.
